text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV-2 - high tail latency detected for customer quicksilver-ai (us-west-2). Alerts: p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 18.7s, streaming stalls observed (~0.9% of streams). Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/generate. Paging oncall.

emma (oncall): ack, I'm on. pulling dashboard + traces. tagging @marta for infra context.

sre-bot: monitors -> https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/streams/quick/quickview?org=us-west-2 (auto-generated link)

raj: I see a sudden spike in KV cache miss rate for the tenant around the same time as latency spike. sample from traces: `kvcache.miss_rate tenant=quicksilver-ai -> 78%` and a queue depth increase on the stream workers.

marta: quick check: tenant is on shared-hosted pool with concurrency burst enabled. customer uses long system prompts and some repeating delimiter tokens (looks like prompt templates that expand). KV cache is getting thrash due to lots of unique prefixes.

emma (oncall): ok mitigation plan (live):
1) move quicksilver-ai traffic to a dedicated reserved pool (quicksilver-pool-2) to isolate noisy primaries.
2) enable per-tenant concurrent request cap = 8 (temporarily).
3) enable fallback routing for streaming -> smaller variant (gpt-small-pp) for excess concurrency.
4) increase streaming idle timeout slightly and reduce batch size to avoid head-of-line stalls.

support-lucy: customer experienced timeouts in their web UI; support contacted them and asked for temporary degraded-mode flag they can enable on their side. Customer is ok with short degrade if we can restore under 5s p99.

deploy-bot: initiated routing change: `POST /internal/routing/policies` payload applied for tenant=quicksilver-ai -> target=quicksilver-pool-2. Operation id: op-9422.

raj: running quick curl to flip concurrency cap and fallback: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://api.redwood.internal/admin/tenants/quicksilver-ai/actions -d '{"set_concurrency_cap":8, "fallback_model":"gpt-small-pp"}'
```
response: 202 accepted, change-id: cid-1177.

emma (oncall): verifying metrics now. initial after-mitigation snapshot (30s after change): p95 0.9s, p99 3.2s, stream stall rate 0.12%. CPU on quicksilver-pool-2 at 60%. queue depth back to baseline. Looks like move helped. :thumbsup:

marta: good. we should still investigate root cause: KV cache key cardinality spiked by ~6x. Hypothesis: customer templates are producing near-unique prefixes due to per-user session ids embedded. Need to consider TTL-based prefix coalescing or normalizing tokens for caching.

raj: pasted a short log snippet from stream-worker showing the stall pattern: ```
[2026-02-12T18:20:03Z] tenant=quicksilver-ai req=abc123 queued_ms=11234 model=gpt-1 stream_state=stall reason=kv-cache-miss
[2026-02-12T18:20:03Z] tenant=quicksilver-ai req=abc124 queued_ms=11500 model=gpt-1 stream_state=stall reason=kv-cache-miss
```

support-lucy: customer reported one of their internal jobs sent a fanout of ~250 concurrent streams after a nightly job misconfigured backoff. they are patching now.

angel: action items for post-incident: 1) reproduce workload in replay infra, 2) add per-tenant prefix cardinality alert, 3) design quick mitigation knobs (auto-throttle + fallback). Assign owners.

emma (oncall): handing off to @marta for overnight oncall at 1759998925. Summary for handoff: incident SEV-2 due to tenant-specific KV cache thrash from high concurrency + unique long prompts -> caused p99 spikes and streaming stalls. Mitigations performed: tenant moved to dedicated pool (quicksilver-pool-2), concurrency cap set to 8, fallback model enabled, temporary batch size reduction. Current state: stabilized p99=3.2s (improving), stream stall ~0.12%, customer in degraded mode but acceptable. Next steps: replay job (raj), postmortem draft (angel), caching improvements (marta).

marta: ack and taking over. I'll keep the routing and caps in place until midnight PST and start the replay job + collect sample prompt set. please tag me if customer reverts or shows regressions.

emma (oncall): thanks everyone. adding short runbook note to the incident ticket and linking to this thread. :white_check_mark:
